A1.justification: Both PDFs describe PriME, with the same authors, core algorithm, and LaMP benchmark. Their complete main texts, equations, tables, figures, and appendices support reliable comparison despite extensive reformatting.

before.justification: V1 reports original LaMP evaluations and privacy, retrieval, LoRA-count, data-sampling, and optimizer analyses, including Appendix C.

after.justification: V2 retains original LaMP results and adds membership-inference evaluations, Llama 3 experiments, and prompt-sensitivity results.

M1.justification: The user embeddings, similarity-based LoRA selection, evolutionary optimization, linear merging, and prediction-similarity penalty remain unchanged. Equations 1–8 and Algorithm 1 retain the same procedure; membership inference evaluates the method rather than becoming a new optimization component.

E1.justification: The same six LaMP personalization tasks remain. V2 extends test scenarios to membership inference on sharing-user training records and GPT-4o-mini-rephrased profiles on LaMP-2 and LaMP-4, without adding a separate dataset or application domain.

E2.justification: Table 1 retains NP, RAG, PAG, Per-Pcs, and OPPU, and the optimizer comparison retains its methods. V2 Table 8 adds Per-Pcs outputs to qualitative comparisons previously limited to PriME variants and the most similar sharing user in v1 Tables 2 and 6.

E3.justification: V2 introduces loss-based membership-inference evaluation with AUC, treating selected sharing users' records as members and averaging across 100 target users. It adds Llama3.1-8B and Llama3.2-3B configurations and controlled profile-rephrasing experiments. V2 Table 7 also exchanges the Per-Pcs batch/top-k labels from v1 Table 3, revising reported settings without establishing that experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: Similarity-based privacy sweeps in v1 Figures 2 and 7 are replaced by attack-based privacy analyses in v2 Tables 2 and 6. V2 adds decoding-stability and profile-phrasing tests and new qualitative cases. The LoRA-count analysis is consolidated but drops LaMP-1; the retrieval, data-sampling, and optimizer analyses largely remain.

E5.justification: V2 Appendix C.3 and Table 9 newly report means and standard errors over three independent decoding runs for RAG/PAG. The profile-rephrasing comparison also specifies a shared decoding seed. This uncertainty reporting is limited to the new prompt analysis.

E6.justification: V2 adds substantial MIA, Llama 3, and prompt-sensitivity results. Table 1 also revises five PriME base entries: LaMP-2 accuracy/F1 change from 0.527/0.398 to 0.523/0.388, LaMP-4 ROUGE-L from 0.180 to 0.179, and LaMP-7 ROUGE-1/ROUGE-L from 0.517/0.463 to 0.520/0.469. These are revised reported values, not established same-setting performance gains.

T1.justification: V2 Section 3.2 explicitly specifies the adversary's black-box access, loss queries, and membership-inference target, adding threat-model assumptions. The mathematical objectives and definitions in Equations 1–8 remain unchanged, and no theorem or proof is added.

C1.justification: V1 presents the privacy-similarity measure as a main contribution. V2 replaces that contribution with a claimed first investigation of membership inference in merging-based personalization and emphasizes attack robustness throughout the abstract, introduction, and conclusion. The evolutionary-personalization and up-to-45% utility claims remain.

C2.justification: V2 interprets privacy through MIA performance and adds qualifications about near-chance AUC, realistic attack evaluation, scalability, and the absence of formal privacy guarantees. It also explains profile-rephrasing failures through altered class labels. V1 Appendix C.1's explanation connecting similar sharing modules to difficult privacy trade-offs is removed.

D1.justification: V2 adds a code-access link, NVIDIA A6000 hardware disclosure, the one-GPU LoRA-training requirement, and attack-implementation details. It explicitly identifies alpha=0 for the main utility results. Much of Appendix B's remaining setup information and Appendix D's prompts already appeared elsewhere in v1.

R1.justification: V2 adds dedicated privacy-risk background covering memorization, membership inference, and privacy across training and prompting, alongside differential-privacy and attribute-inference references. Its positioning shifts toward a claimed first MIA assessment of merging-based personalization. Several earlier PEFT/privacy citations are removed; publication-year updates to retained works are separate bibliographic edits.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, method explanations, results discussion, related work, and conclusion are extensively rewritten. Preliminaries gain numbered subsections, setup details move into Appendix B, prompts move into Appendix D, and separate limitations, ethics, and acknowledgments sections appear.

P2.justification: V2 changes the document template and appendix column layout, replaces privacy plots with tables, consolidates LoRA-count plots into Table 4, and adds several experimental tables. Captions and placements are broadly revised. Two existing headline examples move from v1 Table 6 to v2 Table 3 rather than constituting new results.

improvement.justification: V2 improves empirical breadth and transparency through additional model evaluations, prompt-sensitivity tests, an explicit threat model, reproducibility disclosures, and clearer privacy limitations. However, the central privacy evidence remains problematic: Table 2 treats AUC 0.408 as improved protection without addressing that reversing attack scores yields AUC 0.592. Thus, the additions improve the paper, but do not fully resolve v1's weak support for privacy protection.
